summary.headline: Unicommerce FY26 revenue rose 51.6% to INR204.3 crore, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA growth slowed to 7.8% as investments step up.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 51.6% to INR204.3 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 54.5% to INR43.9 crore, with FY26 being the first full year consolidating Shipway. Q4 revenue grew 14% YoY to INR51.6 crore, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 7.8% to INR9.6 crore and PAT grew 1.6% to INR3.4 crore after management began stepping up growth investments in Q4. Management guided to lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT over the next two quarters, while expecting higher full-year operational profitability in FY27 than FY26. Management also disclosed it is evaluating a merger with Shipway Technology Private Limited.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR35.3 crore at FY25 end
+14% YoY from INR45.3 crore; lower QoQ vs Q3

segments.name: Uniware (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 growth of 11.7%, in line with guidance; management expects double-digit growth in subsequent quarters. Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 37.5% in FY26 from 25% in FY25. Management said the business turned around from about 8% growth in Q3 to double digits in Q4.

segments.name: Shipway
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 growth of 17.7% YoY, with management targeting double-digit growth in FY27 at a faster pace than Uniware. Shipway is not EBITDA positive in Q4 due to sales, marketing and AI investments; management says gross margin is around 20%.

segments.name: International (Uniware)
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in FY26 and is growing faster than India, but contributes about 6-7% of revenue, up from 4-5%. Operates in 7 geographies, with Dubai, Philippines and Malaysia as the priority markets.

segments.name: ConvertWay
segments.commentary: Entry point into the pre-purchase journey; Catalyst AI voice bot is live. No separate financials were disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of double-digit growth for standalone Uniware in FY27 but declined to give a specific growth guidance.
Shipway expected to grow double digits in FY27, faster than Uniware.
Adjusted EBITDA and PAT expected to be lower over the next two quarters (Q1-Q2 FY27) due to growth investments that began in Q4 FY26.
Management expects higher full-year operational profitability in FY27 than FY26, with operating leverage from H2 FY27.
Proposed merger of Unicommerce and Shipway Technology is under evaluation; no timeline given. Management will update the market as the process progresses.
Acquisitions remain a priority: selective targets that are AI-relevant, profitable or near profitability, and available at reasonable valuations; ticket sizes described as not very large.
capex_capacity: Investments started in Q4 FY26 across sales and marketing, AI-led product development, mid-to-senior talent, and AI tools for product and go-to-market, spanning Uniware and Shipway.
Warehouses on the platform can handle 3 lakh to 5 lakh orders daily; peak single-day volume scaled to 55 lakh units from 12 lakh units five years ago.
Platform supports nearly 350 integrations across Uniware, Shipway and ConvertWay, up from about 100 five years ago.
Management said it is no longer publishing shipment or transaction counts; it said it remains above 1 billion transactions.
demand_pricing: Enterprise client onboarding reached 450-plus in FY26, the highest ever; Q4 alone had 149 client additions, also a record. New clients contribute about 7-8% of revenue.
NRR stated as above 100% excluding churn from one top-10 customer that exited due to a change in business model.
Top-10 customer revenue grew about 3.5% YoY; management said existing top-10 contracts have no price escalation yet, which will be rolled out to existing contracts with benefits in later years.
Cross-sell: over 10% of Uniware clients now use Shipway or ConvertWay, up from under 5% overlap at acquisition.
Adoption of newer modules: 40-45% of Uniware enterprise customers use quick commerce and B2B modules; 5-6% adopted UniReco within three quarters; 1-2% adopted UniCapture within a quarter of launch.
Management said the market-growth environment was subdued in FY24-FY25; Q4 seasonality is typically softer than Q3 across both Uniware and Shipway.
Middle East sales cycles lengthened slightly in recent weeks due to regional conflict, reportedly normalizing; India business largely unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Can standalone growth in FY27 be mid-teens, like Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give specific guidance but reiterated confidence in double-digit growth for standalone Uniware, driven by record client acquisition and new product adoption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARPA fall 11% in FY26 despite price escalation clauses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth now relies on new clients and new product adoption as market growth softened; price escalation was added to new contracts from last year and will be extended to existing contracts with benefits in later years.

qa_highlights.question: What is Shipway's FY26 EBITDA margin and steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give Shipway's margin; it said Shipway is not EBITDA positive in Q4 due to investments, while standalone adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 37.5%. Shipway gross margin is about 20% and standalone gross margin about 80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is NRR and the incremental sales and marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: NRR remains above 100% excluding the top-10 churn; new client contribution is 7-8% of revenue. Management did not quantify incremental sales and marketing; it cited investment across sales and marketing, AI talent, AI tools and mid-to-senior hires.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company rely on acquisitions for growth, and what is the target profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions are a core strategy: targets should be relevant to existing customers, AI-relevant, profitable or near profitability, and reasonably valued. Pre-purchase (ConvertWay adjacency) and post-purchase (analytics, loyalty) are white spaces.

qa_highlights.question: How is ESOP expense rising and what dilution should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ESOPs were issued to existing and new mid-to-senior talent, increasing share-based expense; it aims to avoid dilution from acquisitions by using cash instead.

qa_highlights.question: Any slowdown from the Middle East conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: India business has seen little disruption; the Middle East, a small contributor, saw slightly longer sales cycles in recent weeks, which management said are normalising.

risks_watch: Lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT in Q1-Q2 FY27 from investment ramp; FY27 full-year profit recovery depends on H2 operating leverage.
Top-10 customer revenue growth slowed to about 3.5%; one large customer churned due to a business model change.
ARPA decline in FY26 (down 11%) and growth dependent on new product adoption and price escalations in existing contracts.
Shipway's EBITDA is negative in Q4 FY26 and its sequential revenue declined; management has stopped publishing transaction counts.
Proposed Unicommerce–Shipway merger is at evaluation stage with no timeline or terms disclosed.
Share-based payment expense rising; dilution path not quantified.
Management did not give FY27 growth guidance; double-digit is the stated expectation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and Uniware's turnaround, but cautious on near-term profitability, openly flagging lower EBITDA and PAT for two quarters. Management was evasive on specifics: it declined to quantify FY27 growth, Shipway margins, incremental sales and marketing spend, and acquisition revenue models.
key_quotes: We are now an AI-first company.
You will see the near-term financial impact of these investments in the form of lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT over the next 2 quarters.
We are debt-free, cash generative and profitable.
We are currently evaluating the initiation of our merger process between Unicommerce eSolutions Limited and Shipway Technology Private Limited.

growth.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 growth for standalone Uniware (no specific number) and faster double-digit growth for Shipway, plus higher FY27 operational profitability, but backing is qualitative: record 450+ enterprise onboardings and 149 Q4 additions, with no specific capacity, order book or contract figures behind the growth.
